methodologyNotes: Roster covers twelve electric meat/food slicers spanning compact home-use gear-driven units (Chef'sChoice, Cuisinart, Elite Gourmet, Nesco, Ostba, Anescra) to semi-commercial belt-driven machines (KWS, BESWOOD, VEVOR, Kitchener), verified 2026-08-05 primarily against manufacturer product pages (chefschoice.com, cuisinart.com, nesco.com, beswood.com, vevor.com, shopelitegourmet.com) and corroborated by major retailers (Newegg, Target, Home Depot, Best Buy, Walmart, Amazon listing metadata, Woot) and secondary dealer pages (chefequipment.com, cookercooler.com, bigeasymart.com, samstores.com); several retailer product pages (kitchenwarestation.com, agrisupply.com, camelcamelcamel.com, salvionline.com, meatprocessingproducts.com) returned bot-blocked (403), DNS, or connection errors during fetch and were skipped in favor of the corroborating sources actually cited. Where no manufacturer/retailer page disclosed a spec (e.g. weight for the KWS and Cuisinart units, dishwasher-safe status for most units, food carriage dimensions for most compact home units), the field is left null rather than inferred by analogy to similar models. The Chef'sChoice 609A0's price could only be confirmed via a Woot deal-site listing ($84.99, marked sold out at time of check) rather than a standing manufacturer/retailer list price; priceNote flags this explicitly. The Kitchener 9" slicer's only directly-priced listing found (samstores.com, $261.85) is the 220V export variant explicitly marked "NOT FOR USA"; the domestic 120V/belt-driven US version was confirmed to exist via Amazon listing metadata (title only, dynamic price not retrievable) but no standing USD price could be verified, so priceUsd is null for that entry rather than borrowing the export-variant figure. accessedAt 2026-08-05 throughout.
